Data.title: A Fed Rate Hike Next Month Is Almost Certain: Analysts Share Their Views on 2027
Data.body: The probability of a Fed rate hike at its December 9 meeting reached 99% in futures pricing, as reported by Reuters on November 27. A prominent 25 basis point increase would bring the policy rate to the 4.00–4.25% range. Economists are divided on how many more rate hikes will continue into 2027. Capital Economics keeps the possibility of another January hike open, while BNP Paribas expects a hike in March. First Trust, however, believes the market has priced in a large number of hikes for next year. Capital Economics points to January as a possibility, BNP Paribas to March. The Fed kept interest rates stable at 3.75–4.00 percent at its October meeting. Data released after the decision showed annual headline PCE inflation rising from 3.7 percent to 3.8 percent, and core PCE inflation increasing from 3.1 percent to 3.3 percent. The annualized growth forecast for the US economy in the third quarter was also revised upwards from 3.4 percent to 4.3 percent. Capital Economics North America economist Bradley Saunders, in a note dated November 25, stated that based on these two data points, he sees a 25 basis point increase in December as the most likely step, and that a further increase may be necessary in January. Related News: Analyst Benjamin Cowen Believes a Sustained Recovery in Bitcoin Will Come in 2027 BNP Paribas Chief US Economist James Egelhof forecasts a 25 basis point increase at each of the December, January, and March meetings. In this scenario, interest rates would rise to the 4.50–4.75% range in March. According to Egelhof, the economy’s resilience despite high borrowing costs suggests that the neutral interest rate level, which neither accelerates nor slows the economy, may be higher than expected in the short term. Matthew Miskin, an investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, told Reuters on November 27 that weak data could open up room for the Fed to send a more cautious message. The November employment report, to be released Friday, December 4 at 4:30 PM Turkish time, is important in this regard. The LSEG survey expects non-farm payrolls to increase by 90,000, following the 165,000 increase in October, and unemployment to remain at 4.1 percent. The Fed will release its new economic projections along with its interest rate decision on Wednesday, December 9 at 10:00 PM Turkish time. The median interest rate forecast for the end of 2027, which was 4.1 percent in September, will serve as a reference point to gauge expectations of further tightening. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Bitcoin: Another Chance To Buy At Low Prices
Data.body: Summary Bitcoin may be bottoming after falling to $55,000 and recovering above $60,000; the 417-day bear market exceeds prior cycles. Weekly price lows diverge from rising RSI and MACD lines, suggesting a potential trend reversal. Further equity-market declines could push Bitcoin to another lower low; past cycle patterns and the magnitude of future gains are not guaranteed. Consider dollar-cost averaging, IBIT for ETF exposure, or MSTR for leveraged exposure, with an exit strategy to lock in bull-market profits. The price action of Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) has been confusing over the past several months. Many analysts, including myself, thought that Bitcoin bottomed early in this cycle in June 2026 as the price hit about $57k and then rose to over $87k. However, the recent plunge from $87k to about $55k negated that idea. I did state in my last Bitcoin article that the new bull market could be invalidated if the price made a lower low. The recent sell-off in equities likely drove Bitcoin's price down over the same time. Bitcoin has since recovered back above $60k. Bitcoin's technical price perspective on the weekly chart shows a stronger bullish divergence with two lower lows for the price and two higher lows on the RSI. This means that the bottom is more likely to be in from my perspective. Adding to this theory is the amount of time that the bear market lasted. The price of bitcoin peaked on October 6, 2025, at about $126k. We are now about 417 days into this Bitcoin bear market. Bitcoin's bear markets tend to last for about one year. We are already 51 days past one year in this cycle. Here's the length for each of Bitcoin's bear markets: Bitcoin's Previous Bear Markets (charts.bitcoin.com) Prior to this current bear market, the longest one lasted 406 days, which was the 1st cycle. Now, that we are past 406 days in this bear market, a new bull market is likely to be close at hand in my opinion. Technical Perspective BTC-USD ) Weekly Chart w/ RSI & MACD" contenteditable="false" width="640" height="370"> Bitcoin (BTC-USD) Weekly Chart w/ RSI & MACD (TradingView) Bitcoin's weekly chart above displays the bullish divergence that formed in 2026. This is where Bitcoin's price made a lower low in June 2026 and another lower low in November 2026. At the same time, the RSI made two higher lows. The blue MACD line and red signal lines also rose during that time, reinforcing the bullish divergence. Bullish divergences like this typically result in changes in trend back to positive from what I have observed. If we look back at 2022, Bitcoin experienced a similar bullish divergence right before the last bull market. So, strong price rallies could be close at hand as 2026 finishes and 2027 begins. Without the bullish divergence set-up, the RSI is still technically bearish as it remains below the 50 level. The MACD is also bearish, as the blue MACD line is below the red signal line, while the histogram bars are red. However, the bullish divergence set-up should drive these indicators to reverse and turn bullish. The MACD would turn bullish when the blue line rises back above the red signal line while the histogram bars turn green. The bull markets typically last for about three years. So, now is probably a good time to accumulate Bitcoin to benefit from the potential 3-year bull market. The Risks For Bitcoin Bitcoin's price action can be unpredictable as we've witnessed in recent months. The price can make high percentage moves in both directions in short periods of time. There is no guarantee that the price will follow similar patterns as it did in prior price cycles. Future bull markets could also be much lower percentage-wise from the bottom to the peak price as compared to prior cycles. Bitcoin tends to sell-off along with equities. The stock market as measured by the S&P 500 ( SPY ) has been in a correction in October and November of 2026. Bitcoin's recent dip in price occurred during the S&P 500's correction. A continued sell-off in equities could lead to more declines for Bitcoin in the near term. So, it is possible that Bitcoin hits yet another lower price. Strategies For Investors Dollar-cost averaging into Bitcoin at regular intervals (weekly, monthly) during the bottoming process is one strategy for investors to consider. We've seen in recent months how unpredictable the price can be in the short-term. So, trying to get in at the exact bottom may not be feasible. Dollar-cost averaging into Bitcoin can allow investors to build a position near the price lows of this cycle. Investors then benefit when the price of bitcoin rises. Investors can consider buying bitcoin the traditional way with a secure wallet. However, many might prefer to simply buy a bitcoin-based ETF such as the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF ( IBIT ). IBIT tracks the price of bitcoin and can be bought and sold just like any other ETF or stock. IBIT also has options, giving investors more strategies to use, such as covered calls and selling puts. Buying Strategy ( MSTR ) can be a more levered way to trade bitcoin. Strategy currently holds 851,301 bitcoin, or 4% of the total bitcoin supply. Strategy tends to experience higher percentage gains than Bitcoin. Be aware that MSTR also experiences higher percentage losses than Bitcoin. So, having an exit strategy near the end of the bull markets can be wise to lock in profits. That same strategy can be true for IBIT and other bitcoin ETFs.

Data.title: Attention Bitcoin (BTC) Investors! The Death Cross is Back in the Spotlight! Analyst Examines 13 Past Examples!
Data.body: A critical technical signal is approaching that could increase expectations of a decline in the leading cryptocurrency, Bitcoin. Accordingly, a significant technical signal has emerged that could increase expectations of a decline in Bitcoin. In his analysis dated November 27, analyst Omkar Godbole stated that Bitcoin is approaching a death cross, which is considered a harbinger of a downtrend in technical analysis. Examining 13 similar signals from the past, the analyst calculated that the median decline in Bitcoin price until the next golden cross is approximately 24 percent. The Gap Between Bitcoin’s 50 and 200-Day Moving Averages is Narrowing! A death cross occurs when the 50-day simple moving average falls below the 200-day moving average. Technical analysts interpret this development as a bearish signal, indicating that short-term price movements are weaker compared to the long-term trend. According to the analyst, the difference between the two moving averages has narrowed from 12 percent a month ago to 3.45 percent. This narrowing suggests that a death cross may be approaching on the Bitcoin chart. Analyzing 13 historical death crossover data points, the analyst noted that the sharpest declines occurred in 2014 and 2022. Bitcoin lost 66% of its value in 2014 and 64% in 2022. The drop following the 2011 crossover also reached 59%. However, not every death crossover resulted in sharp declines. While Bitcoin only fell by 0.3% following the signal in September 2023, it recorded drops of 2.9% in 2015 and 5.7% in April 2025. The Crossroads of Death Doesn’t Mean a Fall! The analyst emphasizes that the impact of the 13 past examples on BTC is limited and that low market liquidity in previous periods could affect the results. Furthermore, the analyst points out that the death cross is a lagging indicator that appears after a decline has begun, as it is calculated from past price movements, and therefore does not definitively confirm a new wave of selling in Bitcoin. *This is not investment advice. Data.title: Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $7.4 Billion in BTC, Breaking a Nine Year Pattern
Data.body: Key takeaways Balances in Bitcoin addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC from September 30 to November 21, worth about $7.4 billion at a reference price of $61,000. Bitcoin fell 29.5% over the same period. This group reduced its holdings in seven of the previous nine fourth quarters. Its 4.29% increase so far in Q4 2026 is the largest fourth-quarter gain since 2020. The group’s unrealized profit margin dropped from 33.9% to 5.7% by November 21, the lowest reading of 2026 in the report. Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC recorded $2.1 billion in net realized losses through November 21. Exchange inflows from transaction outputs of at least 1,000 BTC also picked up in November. Rising address balances alone cannot establish how much new money entered Bitcoin or whether its price has bottomed. Bitcoin whales have reversed their usual year-end pattern. Between September 30 and November 21, balances in addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC even though Bitcoin lost 29.5% of its value. At a reference price of $61,000, those additional coins are worth roughly $7.4 billion. The figures come from CryptoQuant’s November 27 research report , which was supported by crypto lender CoinRabbit. The study excludes exchange and mining-pool addresses from its balance cohorts. Its findings are a snapshot through November 21, not a final tally for the quarter. The timing matters. NewsBTC recently reported more than $2 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows . Fund withdrawals and rising whale balances point in different directions, but they measure different things. Neither tells us whether the same investors are moving their money from ETFs into direct Bitcoin ownership. A broader measure from Maketo’s whale holdings data puts the balance of addresses with at least 1,000 BTC at 7.22 million BTC on November 26, up 54,379 BTC over the preceding 30 days. That group includes exchange and custody addresses, so it provides a separate view of where coins are held rather than an independent check of CryptoQuant’s 121,117 BTC figure. Bitcoin Whales Reverse Their Year-End Balance Trend The combined balance of the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort at just under 2.95 million BTC on November 21, up from 2.83 million at the end of September. Large addresses reduced their balances in seven of the nine preceding fourth quarters. Only 2019 and 2020 escaped that pattern. The 4.29% increase recorded so far this quarter is the largest Q4 gain since 2020, although December could still change the result. For comparison, the cohort lost nearly 203,000 BTC over Q4 2025. This year’s increase has come during a falling market, rather than a rally. There is a catch in calling this a $7.4 billion accumulation. The figure values the additional coins at a reference price; it does not measure the dollars spent buying them. Transfers between addresses, including movements across the cohort’s balance thresholds, can change the total without a market purchase. The increase tells us where Bitcoin is sitting. It does not tell us how much fresh capital is behind it. That distinction matters when liquidity is scarce. Bitcoin Whales Are Running Out Of Profits To Protect The 121,117 BTC figure makes for a bullish headline. The number I would pay closer attention to is the remaining profit margin. Among addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC, the unrealized profit margin fell from 33.9% at the end of September to 5.7% on November 21, its lowest reading of 2026 in the report. The deterioration is even clearer in dollar terms. Combined unrealized profits for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC stood at about $24 billion on November 21, down from a peak of $294 billion in August 2025. Across the broader group of addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC, net realized losses reached approximately $2.1 billion in the first 52 days of Q4. The on-chain data suggests that some large holders are already moving coins at a loss rather than waiting for a recovery. The relevant distinction is between the balance held at a given date and the profit or loss on coins that move. A growing balance does not prevent other coins within the cohort from being spent below their estimated cost basis. Exchange deposits deserve a closer look, too. Inflows from unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) of at least 1,000 BTC averaged 5,012 BTC per day in November through the report’s cutoff, compared with 3,239 in October. That is a measure of large coin outputs, not a count of individual whales. November’s pickup should not obscure the bigger picture: the quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC per day remained below the 2019–2025 Q4 average of 4,575 BTC. Large deposits are not proof of sales, and a rise in this metric alone does not establish that selling pressure has intensified. What Would Confirm A Bitcoin Market Bottom? The 2018 and 2022 bear markets offer a useful comparison, though not a roadmap for this one. Balances in the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort declined in both of those fourth quarters. Their average unrealized profit margins were negative, while the group still had a positive margin at the November 21 reading this year. Today’s accumulation may be a sign that some large holders are willing to retain exposure through the downturn. The address data cannot establish their motives or identify how much of the increase came from new purchases. I would not call a market bottom on these numbers alone. A further price decline could wipe out the cohort’s remaining profit cushion. Whether that produces more selling depends on the holders’ liquidity needs and positioning, neither of which can be read directly from address balances. The next test is whether large-address balances keep rising while net realized losses and large exchange deposits ease. That combination, alongside evidence of renewed spot demand, would make the recovery case more convincing. For now, the change in year-end positioning is real within CryptoQuant’s measured cohort. Evidence of a durable recovery is still missing.

Data.title: Why Is Silver Price Surging Today? Silver Futures Jump 10% as Gold Reclaims $3,600
Data.body: Key takeaways Silver futures surge 10% following Wednesday's dramatic selloff Gold reclaims $3,600 as investors return to metals Persistent inflation and rate hike expectations threaten recovery Silver futures surged more than 10% to $44.17 per ounce on Friday, November 27, as investors returned to precious metals following a turbulent week. Gold futures climbed nearly 4% to $3,675, while copper also participated in the broader commodity market recovery. The rally follows Wednesday's selloff, when silver approached $38 per ounce and gold dropped below $3,500 . Silver has subsequently recovered approximately 16% from that reference level, although it remains significantly below its January record. The sharp rebound has occurred despite persistent expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December. Why Is Silver Outperforming Gold Today? Improving risk appetite, easing dollar pressure and renewed buying following recent losses appear to be supporting Friday's recovery. The broader Black Friday market rally has also seen investors return to equities following several volatile trading sessions. Silver's dual role as both a precious and industrial metal makes it particularly sensitive to changes in economic sentiment. Unlike gold, which primarily attracts investment and jewelry demand, silver is extensively used in electronics, automotive components and renewable energy infrastructure. Reduced trading activity following Thanksgiving may also be amplifying price movements, allowing relatively modest changes in buying pressure to generate substantial gains. Nevertheless, the recovery follows several unsuccessful rebound attempts, including Monday's 7% silver rally , which failed to prevent prices from subsequently reaching fresh annual lows. Silver Faces a 35 Million Ounce Supply Deficit Despite its substantial price correction, silver continues to face a structural imbalance between physical supply and demand. According to the Silver Institute , global silver demand is projected to exceed supply by 35 million ounces in 2026, marking the sixth consecutive year of market deficits. Industrial consumption outside the photovoltaic sector is forecast to increase by 4.5% to 492 million ounces. However, declining solar-sector consumption is expected to contribute to a 3% reduction in overall industrial demand. Meanwhile, global silver-backed exchange-traded product holdings had declined by 55 million ounces since the beginning of 2026 as of November 3. This helps explain why silver can experience substantial price declines despite persistent physical shortages. Investment outflows can release previously accumulated metal into the market, temporarily easing supply constraints. Silver Price Forecast: Can Silver Reclaim $50? Silver futures remain approximately 64% below January's record price of $121.65, illustrating the scale of the broader correction despite Friday's recovery. The immediate challenge is establishing momentum above $45, a level previously identified as an important recovery threshold . Reclaiming $50 would require an additional rally of approximately 13% from Friday's $44.17 reference price. However, accelerating US inflation remains a significant obstacle. The latest PCE inflation figures showed annual inflation reaching 3.8% in October, reinforcing expectations of monetary tightening.

Data.title: Two December Events Could Determine Whether the US Stock Market Ends 2026 in Recovery
Data.body: Key takeaways November employment figures could reshape interest rate expectations Federal Reserve faces its final policy decision of 2026 Higher borrowing costs threaten a sustained stock market recovery The US stock market faces two critical tests in December that could determine whether Wall Street extends its recent recovery or experiences another wave of selling before the end of 2026. The November employment report, scheduled for December 4, and the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on December 9 could redirect investor attention from the recent turmoil surrounding Nvidia toward the broader economic outlook. Despite Monday's stock market rally , the S&P 500 remains substantially below its October record, while the Nasdaq continues to struggle with a deeper technology sector correction. December 4: Strong Employment Could Become Bad News for Stocks According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics , the US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, while unemployment remained at 4.1%. September's employment growth was also revised upward from 29,000 to 60,000. November's employment figures will provide policymakers with another indication of whether the economy can withstand higher borrowing costs. While strong employment typically supports corporate earnings and consumer spending, it could also strengthen the argument for monetary tightening. October's labor market figures already contributed to rising rate hike expectations . A substantial slowdown in hiring could ease pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates aggressively. However, unexpectedly weak employment figures could introduce a different concern: deteriorating economic conditions and weaker corporate earnings. For equity investors, moderate employment growth without accelerating wage pressures may represent the most favorable outcome. December 9: The Fed's Final Interest Rate Decision The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.75-4.00% during its October meeting, according to its official policy statement . However, two policymakers voted in favor of a 25-basis-point increase, highlighting growing concerns about persistent inflation. The December meeting will also feature updated economic projections, giving investors insight into policymakers' expectations for interest rates, inflation, employment and economic growth in 2027. A widely anticipated rate increase may already be partially reflected in equity valuations. Consequently, the market's reaction could depend more heavily on whether the Fed signals additional increases next year. Recent inflation figures have complicated the outlook, making a sustained return to monetary easing less certain. Can the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Recover Before 2027? Technology companies remain particularly exposed to rising interest rates because their valuations often depend on expectations of future earnings. Higher discount rates reduce the present value of those earnings, while increasing financing costs for capital-intensive projects. The recent AI stock selloff demonstrates how sensitive the Nasdaq has become to changing expectations surrounding artificial intelligence investment. Companies financing expensive data centers could face additional pressure if borrowing costs remain elevated throughout 2027. Meanwhile, more diversified indexes may benefit from investors rotating into businesses with established cash flows and lower financing requirements. The recent Dow Jones recovery offers an example of how differently major US indexes can respond to changing market conditions.

Data.title: Why Is Nvidia Stock Lagging the Nasdaq Despite Jensen Huang's Return as CEO?
Data.body: Key takeaways Nvidia underperforms the Nasdaq despite Huang's return Corporate investigations continue following the CEO's reinstatement AI infrastructure spending remains central to valuation concerns Nvidia ( NASDAQ: NVDA ) struggled to participate in Friday's technology stock recovery, trading around $149 while the Nasdaq Composite gained approximately 0.8%. The divergence suggests that Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive has not resolved the broader concerns weighing on the semiconductor giant. NVDA remains nearly 10% below Monday's closing price of $165.05, when its extraordinary 31.5% rally helped trigger a historic market recovery . Shares also remain approximately 39% below their October record high of $243.37. The reversal raises an important question: was Nvidia's leadership crisis ever the primary reason behind its declining valuation? Jensen Huang's Return Has Not Eliminated Regulatory Risks According to Nvidia's official announcement , the board unanimously supported Huang's reinstatement after discussions with the executive and consultations with senior US government officials. However, Nvidia confirmed that its independent investigation would continue. The company has also established a National Security and Export Control Committee and begun searching for a chief compliance officer. These measures indicate that Huang's return resolved immediate leadership uncertainty without necessarily eliminating longer-term regulatory and corporate governance risks. Monday's optimism subsequently gave way to another AI stock selloff , with Nvidia closing Tuesday at $155.38 before slipping to $149.30 on Wednesday. By comparison, the Nasdaq Composite declined approximately 2.1% across those two sessions, considerably less than Nvidia's 9.5% loss. Nvidia's $115.8 Billion Revenue Masks a Growing Exposure Nvidia's underlying business continues to expand rapidly. Its latest quarterly results showed revenue increasing 103% year-over-year to $115.8 billion, while net income reached $65.3 billion. However, data center sales accounted for approximately 93% of total revenue, making Nvidia particularly sensitive to changes in corporate AI infrastructure budgets. Unlike the diversified Nasdaq Composite, Nvidia depends heavily on customers continuing to purchase increasingly expensive computing systems. Any slowdown in data center construction, financing availability or demand for computing capacity could therefore have an outsized impact on its growth expectations. The company's record quarterly earnings also came alongside expectations of declining gross margins and a fourth-quarter revenue forecast that excludes data center computing sales in China. Meanwhile, persistent inflation pressures threaten to keep borrowing costs elevated, potentially making debt-financed AI infrastructure projects less economically attractive. Can Nvidia Stock Recover Its Lost Momentum? Nvidia retains significant financial resources, including approximately $227.3 billion in unused share repurchase authorization. Its next-generation Vera Rubin platform and expanding relationships with major cloud providers also support its long-term growth prospects. Nevertheless, the recent technology market correction suggests that investors are reassessing the relationship between AI infrastructure expenditure and sustainable investment returns.

Data.title: Software Engineer: The Closest I Will Ever Get to Predicting XRP Price
Data.body: Vincent Van Code (@vincent_vancode), a software engineer and recognized voice in the XRP community, recently shared what he called his closest attempt at predicting XRP’s price. He was careful to separate it from a formal prediction. “This is not a prediction,” he wrote , describing it instead as “my educated guess if everything goes as Ripple planned.” Van Code is estimating what XRP would need to be worth for Ripple’s stated strategic goals to function at scale. Breaking Down the Numbers Van Code linked to an older post where he laid out his reasoning in full. His starting point is Ripple’s GTreasury customer base. He believes those customers alone handle payments across global economies with multiple currency pairs. That activity requires deep liquidity pools. Van Code estimates the total payment volume at $13 trillion, with $3 trillion attributed to Hidden Roads, bringing the full figure to $16 trillion across the network . From there, he argues that if 30% of that $16 trillion in payment volume moves onto XRP and the XRP Ledger, the price would rise to $15-$20 . He sets an estimated timeframe of the end of 2027 for that stage. This is the closest I will ever get to predicting $XRP price… but its not a prediction, just my educated guess if everything goes as Ripple planned. https://t.co/vs2RDJG7oT — Vincent Van Code (@vincent_vancode) November 25, 2026 Van Code’s Long-Term View Looking further ahead, Van Code estimates that by 2030, if that volume is fully migrated and an additional $10 trillion comes onto the network, XRP’s value would reach $500-$600. He is explicit that this is “an estimate of price based on the strategic payment volume Ripple is intending to migrate over.” He acknowledges uncertainty, writing, “Whether the price pumps accordingly, how much and by when, I got no idea dude, no one does, not even Ripple.” The Community’s Response The post drew a range of reactions from the XRP community. One response pushed back on the payments narrative, arguing that XRP’s real value lies in its role as institutional collateral rather than as a payment coin. He laid out a detailed case for how locked XRP reduces free float, increases price per unit, and serves large-scale obligations in credit, margin, and settlement. Another commenter expressed broad agreement with Van Code’s overall position, calling his social media presence one of the most valuable in the XRP space. One response put a single price figure of $589 on the table. Many in the community strongly believe that XRP can hit $589 and that target has circulated for years. The post Software Engineer: The Closest I Will Ever Get to Predicting XRP Price appeared first on Times Tabloid .

Data.title: Anthropic Stock Jumps 7%, Reclaims $83 IPO Price as AI Stocks Rise
Data.body: Key takeaways Anthropic shares recover above their $83 IPO price AI stocks rebound following several volatile trading sessions Infrastructure costs and upcoming share unlocks remain risks Anthropic stock ( NASDAQ: ANT ) jumped nearly 7% to $88.33 during Friday's morning trading, reclaiming its $83 initial public offering price as investors returned to beaten-down artificial intelligence stocks following the Thanksgiving holiday. The recovery comes after a turbulent first week on Nasdaq, during which the Claude developer lost its entire IPO premium. Anthropic had previously struggled to participate in the broader technology rally despite renewed demand for semiconductor and AI infrastructure stocks. Friday's rebound puts investors who purchased shares at the offering price back in positive territory, although ANT remains approximately 23% below its debut-day high of $115.10. Anthropic Stock Recovers After Record $93.5 Billion IPO According to Anthropic's official announcement , its initial public offering generated approximately $93.5 billion in gross proceeds after underwriters fully exercised their additional share purchase option. The company also raised $26 billion through a concurrent private placement involving seven technology companies, including Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Google and Broadcom. Combined gross proceeds reached approximately $119.5 billion, including shares sold by existing shareholders. Despite substantial institutional interest, including Cathie Wood's investment through six ARK exchange-traded funds, Anthropic's stock experienced heavy selling pressure following its public debut. ANT opened at $111.50 on November 19 before closing its first session at $97.17. Shares subsequently fell as low as $73.85 before recovering above their offering price on Friday. AI Stock Recovery Faces a Profitability Test Anthropic's rebound follows a volatile week in which AI stocks experienced renewed selling pressure amid concerns over technology valuations, infrastructure financing and future profitability. Anthropic's financial disclosures illustrate why investors remain sensitive to these risks. Its SEC prospectus revealed that revenue reached $33.2 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $2.5 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. Computing and infrastructure expenses increased from $4.4 billion to $18.8 billion over the same period. However, those expenses declined from 172% of revenue to approximately 57%, suggesting that revenue growth is beginning to outpace computing costs. The improvement represents an important development for Anthropic, although it does not eliminate the company's other operating expenses or guarantee future profitability. Meanwhile, elevated Treasury yields remain a challenge for technology companies whose valuations depend heavily on projected earnings. Can Anthropic Stock Return Above $100? Reclaiming the $83 offering price marks an important psychological milestone for ANT. A sustained recovery could bring its first-day closing price of $97.17 and the $100 threshold back into focus. However, another potential catalyst is approaching. Up to 303 million shares could become eligible for sale through a scheduled share unlock on December 15. The expiration of selling restrictions does not guarantee that shareholders will immediately dispose of their holdings, but it could increase the supply of publicly tradable shares.

Data.title: Paul Tudor Jones Doubles Bitcoin (BTC) ETF Stake to $64.6M in Q3
Data.body: Paul Tudor Jones's Tudor Investment doubled its Bitcoin ETF stake to 1.36 million IBIT shares, worth $64.6 million, its Q3 13F filing shows.
